descriptors.definition: Ind AS 107 prescribes financial instrument disclosures that allow users to assess their importance to an entity's financial position and performance. It also requires reporting the nature, extent, and management of risks arising from these instruments during and at the end of the reporting period.
inclusion: Disclosures enabling evaluation of financial instrument significance
Disclosures detailing risk exposures and risk management strategies
exclusion: Recognition and measurement criteria of financial instruments
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from recognition rules under Ind AS 109 by focusing exclusively on qualitative and quantitative communication to financial statement users

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide disclosures that enable financial statement users to evaluate how significantly financial instruments impact overall financial position and performance. This entails breaking down carrying amounts and gains or losses across specific categorization standards.
inclusion: Information allowing users to assess the importance of financial instruments to financial position
Information allowing evaluation of performance impacts
exclusion: Operational management narratives unrelated to financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on overall significance rather than standalone fair value measurement mechanics

descriptors.concept_name: Balance Sheet Disclosures for Financial Instruments
descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the carrying amounts of financial assets and liabilities categorized under various valuation paradigms either directly on the balance sheet or within the notes. These categories include items measured at fair value through profit or loss, amortized cost, and fair value through other comprehensive income.
terminology: Fair Value through Profit or Loss
Fair Value through Other Comprehensive Income
inclusion: Carrying amounts of financial assets and liabilities at fair value through profit or loss
Financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income
nearby_distinctions: Differs from statement of profit and loss disclosures by focusing on stock balances rather than flow items of income and expense

descriptors.concept_name: Statement of Profit and Loss Disclosures for Financial Instruments
descriptors.definition: Entities are required to disclose net gains or losses, interest revenue and expense calculated via the effective interest method, and fee income and expense associated with financial instruments either in comprehensive income statements or notes. These breakdowns must separate items by valuation category such as amortized cost and fair value through profit or loss.
inclusion: Net gains or losses on financial assets and liabilities by measurement category
Total interest revenue and expense using effective interest method
Fee income and expense arising from non-FVPL assets and liabilities and fiduciary activities
nearby_distinctions: Captures flow statements of financial performance and periodic earnings rather than static period-end asset and liability balances

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose significant accounting policies, hedge accounting strategies, cash flow impacts, and detailed fair value comparisons alongside unrecognised initial gains or losses. This ensures comprehensive reporting transparency regarding risk management strategies and valuation inputs.
inclusion: Significant accounting policies and measurement bases
Hedge accounting risk management strategies and financial statement effects
Fair value comparisons by class and initial unrecognised gain or loss reconciliations
exclusion: Basic balance sheet carrying amount line-item totals
nearby_distinctions: Supplements primary financial statement line-item disclosures with qualitative risk metrics, valuation policy reconciliations, and hedge accounting specifics
